title: 50 storey residential tower, Brisbane CBD: structural steel
workplace: 50 storey residential tower with foyer and 3 level basement carpark, Brisbane CBD
note: Facts are example inputs for testing. On a real project they come from the contractor's own procedures and the project's documents.

swms.title: Roof and plant platform steel erection
swms.task: Erect structural steel for the roof plant platforms and the crown, lifted by the tower crane, connecting and bolting from boom lifts.

facts.erectionSequence: Steel is erected to the designer's sequence on drawing ST-10 (revision C), with temporary bracing as shown, and our supervisor checks each bay is braced before rigging is released.
facts.fallControl: Connectors work from boom lifts with harnesses clipped to the platform anchor point, and edge protection stays in place at the roof edge.
facts.harnessSystem: Workers wear a full body harness with a restraint lanyard short enough that they cannot be thrown from the basket, clipped to the boom lift anchor point. Harnesses and lanyards are checked by the user before each use and inspected by a competent person every 6 months, recorded on the tag. Users are trained in working at heights and boom lift operation by a registered training organisation.

steps: Lift and land steel with the crane company
Erect and connect steel at height

swms.title: Welding steel canopies and stairs
swms.task: Install and weld the steel canopies and steel stairs at the podium, working from scissor lifts.

facts.hotWorkPermit: The principal contractor issues a hot work permit each day, with a fire extinguisher at each work area and a fire watch after hot work ends.
facts.erectionSequence: Canopy and stair steel is installed to the designer's sequence on drawing ST-20 (revision A), propped until all connections are welded.
facts.fallControl: Scissor lifts with guardrails are used for all work above 2 m.
